objective_pt: Comparar costumes de países diferentes e contar como foi se adaptar a eles com "be used to" e "get used to".

teacher.goal_pt: Conversar sobre viagens e ver como o aluno fala de lugares que já visitou.
prompts: What's the most interesting place you've ever been to?
Is there a country you'd love to visit?
watchFor: Dizer "I know Paris" querendo dizer "já fui a Paris"; o natural é "I've been to Paris".
Dizer "I made a travel"; o substantivo contável é "trip".

exercises.prompt: I've been to Portugal twice, but I've never been to Asia.
accepted: I've been to Portugal twice, but I've never been to Asia.
I have been to Portugal twice, but I have never been to Asia.

exercises.instruction_pt: "Eu fiz uma viagem incrível." Which is correct?
options: I went on an amazing trip.
exercises.explanation_pt: "Travel" geralmente é verbo ou substantivo incontável. Para "uma viagem", use "a trip", com "go on" ou "take".

exercises.instruction_pt: Say it in English: "Eu não conheço o Japão, mas adoraria ir."
accepted: I've never been to Japan, but I'd love to go
I have never been to Japan, but I would love to go
I've never been to Japan, but I'd love to go there
I haven't been to Japan, but I'd love to go
I've never been to Japan, but I'd love to
I've never visited Japan, but I'd love to go
I haven't been to Japan yet, but I'd love to go
I've never been to Japan, but I would love to visit

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Conhecer" um lugar, no sentido de ter visitado, é "have been to": "I've never been to Japan".
commonErrors.correction_en: I've never been to Japan, but I'd love to go.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: Para visitas, o mais natural é "been to". "Been in Japan" sugere que você ficou lá um tempo.
commonErrors.correction_en: I've never been to Japan, but I'd love to go.

teacher.goal_pt: Aprender vocabulário de cultura: custom, culture shock, tip, local, etiquette, stand out.
prompts: What surprised you the most in another country?
watchFor: Usar "costume" querendo dizer "costume" (hábito); em inglês é "custom". "Costume" é fantasia.

exercises.example_en: In Japan, it's a custom to take off your shoes at home.
I had a bit of a culture shock when I moved to Germany.
It took me months to get used to the cold.

exercises.instruction_pt: Match each word to its meaning.
Say it in English: "Lá é costume dar gorjeta de 20%."
accepted: It's customary to tip 20% there
It's a custom to tip 20% there
There, it's customary to tip 20%
There it's common to tip 20%
It's common to tip 20% there
People usually tip 20% there
People normally leave a 20% tip there
It's normal to leave a 20% tip there
It's customary to leave a 20% tip there
It's customary to tip twenty percent there
People usually tip twenty percent there

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Costume" em inglês é fantasia. "É costume" é "it's customary", "it's a custom" ou "it's common".
O mais natural é "tip 20%" ou "leave a 20% tip". "Give a tip of" é tradução literal.

teacher.goal_pt: Treinar o som "tch" de "culture" e "adventure" e a diferença entre "used to" (iúsTU) e "use".
watchFor: Pronunciar o "d" de "used to"; na fala vira "iús-tu".

exercises.prompt: Learning about a new culture is a real adventure.
accepted: Learning about a new culture is a real adventure.

exercises.prompt: I'm used to spicy food now, but I wasn't at first.
accepted: I'm used to spicy food now, but I wasn't at first.
I am used to spicy food now, but I was not at first.

exercises.instruction_pt: Which word has the same "ch" sound as "culture"?
exercises.explanation_pt: "Nature" e "culture" têm o som "tch". Em "machine" o "ch" soa "sh", e em "character" soa "k".

teacher.goal_pt: Entender relatos de diferenças culturais e reagir comparando com o Brasil.
prompts: What's different about greetings in Brazil?
What would surprise a foreigner in Brazil?
watchFor: Confundir "I used to" (costumava) com "I'm used to" (estou acostumado).
Dizer "in Brazil is common" sem o "it".

exercises.instruction_pt: Listen. What does the speaker find strange now?
exercises.listen: After living in London for five years, I'm used to queuing. Now when I visit Brazil, it feels strange that people don't queue at the bus stop.
options: People not queuing at the bus stop
exercises.explanation_pt: "I'm used to queuing" = já se acostumou a fazer fila. Por isso estranha quando as pessoas não fazem fila.

exercises.instruction_pt: Listen and answer about how people greet each other in Brazil.
exercises.listen: How do people usually greet each other in Brazil?
accepted: People usually kiss on the cheek
People usually give each other a kiss on the cheek
We usually kiss on the cheek
We usually give a kiss on the cheek
We usually hug or kiss on the cheek
People usually hug and kiss on the cheek
They usually kiss on the cheek
With a kiss on the cheek
With a hug or a kiss on the cheek
We usually greet each other with a kiss on the cheek
In Brazil, people usually kiss on the cheek
In Brazil, it's common to kiss on the cheek

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Beijo no rosto" é "a kiss on the cheek". "Face" soa estranho aqui.
commonErrors.correction_en: People usually kiss on the cheek.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: O inglês precisa de sujeito: "In Brazil, it's common to...".
commonErrors.correction_en: In Brazil, it's common to kiss on the cheek.

exercises.instruction_pt: Listen and answer: is she used to the weather now?
exercises.listen: When I moved to Canada, the winters were awful. But after a couple of years, I got used to them.
accepted: Yes, she is
Yes
Yes, she got used to them
Yes, she got used to it
Yes, she's used to them now
Yes, she's used to it now
Yes, she's used to the winters now
Yes, after a couple of years
Yes, she got used to the winters

commonErrors.explanation_pt: Depois de "be/get used to" vem substantivo ou verbo com -ing: "she's used to the cold", "used to living there".
commonErrors.correction_en: Yes, she's used to them now.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Ela se acostumou" é "she got used to it". "Accustomed" existe ("she became accustomed to"), mas não sozinho como verbo.
commonErrors.correction_en: Yes, she got used to them.

teacher.goal_pt: Contar uma experiência de choque cultural e comparar com o Brasil.
prompts: Have you ever experienced culture shock?
What was hard to get used to?
What would a tourist need to know before visiting Brazil?
watchFor: Dizer "I'm used to wake up early"; depois de "be used to" vem -ing.

exercises.instruction_pt: Say it in English: "Eu não estou acostumado a jantar tão cedo."
accepted: I'm not used to having dinner so early
I'm not used to eating dinner so early
I'm not used to having dinner this early
I'm not used to eating dinner this early
I am not used to having dinner so early
I'm not used to dining so early
I'm not used to having dinner that early
I'm not used to eating so early

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Be used to" é seguido de verbo com -ing: "I'm not used to having dinner". Sem o -ing, vira "used to" (costumava).
commonErrors.correction_en: I'm not used to having dinner so early.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: Com "accustomed to" também vem -ing: "accustomed to having". Mais natural: "I'm not used to having dinner so early".
commonErrors.correction_en: I'm not used to having dinner so early.

exercises.instruction_pt: Say it in English: "Se você for ao Brasil, não deixe de provar pão de queijo."
accepted: If you go to Brazil, make sure you try pão de queijo
If you go to Brazil, make sure to try pão de queijo

If you go to Brazil, be sure to try pão de queijo
If you visit Brazil, make sure you try pão de queijo
If you visit Brazil, don't miss pão de queijo
If you ever go to Brazil, you have to try pão de queijo
When you go to Brazil, make sure you try cheese bread
If you go to Brazil, make sure you try cheese bread
If you go to Brazil, you have to try cheese bread
If you go to Brazil, make sure you try pao de queijo
If you go to Brazil, you have to try pao de queijo
If you go to Brazil, don't forget to try pao de queijo

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Não deixe de" não é "don't leave". Use "make sure you...", "don't forget to..." ou "you have to...".
commonErrors.correction_en: If you go to Brazil, make sure you try pão de queijo.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: Depois de "if" usamos o presente: "If you go to Brazil".
commonErrors.correction_en: If you go to Brazil, make sure you try pão de queijo.
If you go to Brazil, make sure you try pão de queijo.

accepted: It took me a while to get used to the food

exercises.instruction_pt: Talk about a cultural difference you noticed while traveling, or one a foreigner would notice in Brazil.
exercises.prompt_en: I'm visiting Brazil next month for the first time. What should I know about the culture?
guidelines_pt: Give two or three tips: "It's common to...", "People usually..."
Compare: "Unlike in the US, in Brazil..."
Use "get used to": "You'll get used to... quickly."

teacher.goal_pt: Revisar "used to", "be used to" e "get used to" e os falsos cognatos da unidade.
prompts: What did you use to do as a child that you don't do now?
What are you used to doing every morning?
watchFor: "I know Paris" no sentido de ter visitado.

exercises.instruction_pt: Say it in English: "Eu costumava viajar muito antes de ter filhos."
accepted: I used to travel a lot before I had kids
I used to travel a lot before I had children
I used to travel a lot before having kids
I used to travel a lot before having children
I used to travel much more before I had kids
Before I had kids, I used to travel a lot
Before having children, I used to travel a lot

commonErrors.explanation_pt: Para hábitos do passado, use "used to" + verbo: "I used to travel".
commonErrors.correction_en: I used to travel a lot before I had kids.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: Depois de "before" use -ing ("before having") ou uma frase completa ("before I had").
commonErrors.correction_en: I used to travel a lot before having kids.

exercises.sentence: It took me a year to get used to ___ on the left.
accepted: driving

commonErrors.explanation_pt: Depois de "get used to", o verbo vai com -ing: "get used to driving".
commonErrors.correction_en: It took me a year to get used to driving on the left.

exercises.instruction_pt: Which sentence means "Eu já estou acostumado com o frio"?
exercises.explanation_pt: "I'm used to" = estou acostumado. "I used to" + verbo = eu costumava.

exercises.prompt: Traveling opens your mind to new ways of living.
accepted: Traveling opens your mind to new ways of living.
Travelling opens your mind to new ways of living.
Travel opens your mind to new ways of living.
